intro: Someone left the minus-eighty open overnight, and the postdocs arrived to find half the samples ruined, the other half muttering under their foil. Dr Okafor says the DNA never lies, but the freezers have started gossiping, and nobody trusts a clean read now. In the corner, a whiteboard lists the night's corrections in neat red pen, each struck line replaced by something almost right. The postdocs keep their failed runs in labelled tubes along the back shelf, a quiet archive of near-misses folded into their gloves and lab books. You can still hear the samples talking if you stand still long enough; the trick is learning which voice to ignore.
echo: Somewhere in this building, everything is read three letters at a time.
